p4_b1.ocr: TABLE 5: Physicians’ advice to patients who exercised during the first and second trimesters regarding the duration and/or intensity of aerobic and strength- conditioning exercise during the third trimester

p4_b2.ocr: Advice regarding maximum heart rate and perceived exertion Participants were surveyed on their recommendations regarding maximum heart rate (bpm) and level of perceived exertion during an exercise session (Table 6). More than half (54%; n=37) recommend pregnant patients limit exercise based upon heart rate, most commonly 121-140 bpm (25%; n=17) or 141-160 bpm (24%; n=16), whereas 46% ( n=31) do not advise an upper heart rate limit. Also, more than half of physicians (59%; n=40) believe perceived exertion should be somewhat hard, while one-fourth (27%; n=18) advise no limit to exercise based upon perceived exertion.
